title: Two-member rigid plane frame with a loaded joint

source.work: McGuire, W., Gallagher, R. H., Ziemian, R. D., Matrix Structural Analysis
source.notes: input data and targets read on the cited pages; nothing of the source is reproduced

analysis: Plane (x-y) problem of the source modelled in 3D with the global Y axis vertical, so that the source's x, y and theta_z are the model's X, Y and rz. In-plane bending is about local z for every member (default orientation), hence the source's I is the section's Iz. Beam ab horizontal, 8 m (A = 6e3 mm^2, I = 200e6 mm^4); column bc vertical, 5 m, c below b (A = 4e3 mm^2, I = 50e6 mm^4): a (0, 0), b (8, 0), c (8, -5) m. a and c fixed. E = 200,000 MPa. Loads at b: 100 kN at 45 deg (+100/sqrt 2 in x, -100/sqrt 2 in y) and a moment of 50 kN m, counter-clockwise (the solution uses 50 x 10^3 kN mm; the problem figure prints the unit as 'kN'). First order, axial deformation included. Section properties the source does not give because they do not enter its plane model (Iy, J; A where stated) are placeholders that do not influence the targets.

quarantine.diagnosis: u_b and v_b missed by 1.4 and 1.8 times the tolerance: engine 0.44147 and -0.39989 mm, printed 0.4414 and -0.3998 mm (rotation reproduced). Cause: the printed values are truncated, not rounded. Evidence: the exact solution of the source's own printed 3 x 3 equations is 0.44147, -0.39988 mm, 0.0016943 rad - the engine's values; rounded to four digits they would print as 0.4415 and -0.3999. The policy (half a unit in the last printed digit) assumes rounding. The engine's results for this model are confirmed by the other tiers that apply (tier C: OpenSeesPy and PyNite agree with the engine; tier D: equilibrium and the other invariants pass); the difference is between the source's printed digits and the exact solution of the stated problem.
